column2: Retain the hearing command, divine announcement, tomorrow at this hour, one measure of fine flour and two of barley, each for a shekel at Samaria's gates. Will sell supplies the natural commercial predicate; no modern measure conversion is introduced.

Retain both presentatives, the officer supporting the king, future floodgates statement and negative question. The response promises sight but denies eating. The selected wording is not silently changed into even if the Lord made floodgates; the skeptical question's force remains provisional.
column3: Does the negative question mean this cannot happen or can this happen, and how does it connect to the preceding affirmative future about floodgates?

column2: Retain four leprous men beside the city doorway and the question about waiting to die. The account identifies their condition without supplying a particular quarantine rule or a modern clinical diagnosis.

Retain the alternatives of entering the famine-stricken city, staying to die or surrendering to Syria, with both possible outcomes of survival and death. Throw ourselves upon interprets empesomen in context; no guaranteed mercy is implied.

Retain departure in darkness, arrival at part of Syria's camp and the presentative absence of anyone. The selected darkness is not narrowed to a precise twilight hour, nor part changed to a confidently identified perimeter.

Retain the Lord causing the camp to hear chariot, horse and great-force sounds. The Syrians' explanation names plural Hittite kings and Egyptian kings as hired enemies; it is their mistaken inference, not proof those armies were present.
Retain the flight in darkness, abandoned tents, horses and donkeys, the camp left as it was and flight for their lives. The animals remain in camp rather than becoming the fugitives' mounts.

Retain the first tent's food, drink, silver, gold and clothing, then a return to another tent and hiding what was taken. The selected first departure has no explicit hiding verb; one is not inserted to make the two visits identical.

Retain the self-rebuke, day of good news, silence until morning light and encounter with lawlessness. Lawlessness preserves anomia without assuming an explicit punishment or guilt-finding formula; the report to the king's house remains the proposed remedy.
column3: Does finding lawlessness mean incurring guilt, encountering punishment or another consequence, and how should the silence/waiting clauses be connected?

column2: Retain the report to the gate, no man or human voice, tethered horse and donkey, and unchanged tents. The singular equipment/animal wording follows the selected description; the English does not add an unmentioned enemy detachment.
Retain the plural gatekeepers' cry and report inside the king's house. The unit distinguishes the city's entry officials from the men who discovered the camp; no personal messenger name is supplied.

Retain the king rising at night and his proposed Syrian ambush explanation based on Israel's hunger. Their imagined speech is nested within his inference; the narrator has already given a different cause, which is not overwritten.

Retain the proposed five remaining horses, presentative, comparison with Israel's failing multitude and sending to investigate. Like supplies the comparison implicit in pros; the selected shorter clause is not expanded into two familiar comparisons with living and dead Israelites.
column3: What is the exact comparison between the remaining horses and Israel's failing multitude, and does failing sufficiently convey the participle ekleipon?

column2: Retain two horse riders, not two chariots, sent after the king of Syria with the instruction to go and see. This execution of the reconnaissance proposal is not numerically harmonized with the five horses just requested.

Retain pursuit as far as the Jordan, Behold, the whole road filled with discarded garments and equipment, panic, and the messengers' return. The road evidence confirms flight without an added account of a battle.

Retain the people's plundering and both prices exactly matching the initial announcement: one measure of fine flour and two barley measures, each a shekel. The Lord's word is the stated fulfillment reference.

Retain the officer's gate appointment, repeated arm-support description, crowd trampling and death. The timing reference says messenger came down, not king; that selected identity remains despite the dialogue's royal context.

Retain the repeated price prediction with barley first and fine flour second, unlike verse 1's order. Will be available supplies the English predicate for the commodity-price statement; tomorrow at this hour and Samaria's gate remain.

Retain the recalled officer's present makes floodgates, unlike will make in verse 2, and the same negative question and sight-without-eating reply. Repetition is intentional narrative fulfillment, not duplicate material to remove.
column3: The same negative-question issue as verse 2 remains open; the present/future variation should not be silently standardized while resolving it.

column2: Retain the explicit fulfillment, repeated trampling at the gate and death. The closing repetition emphasizes the outcome and is not shortened to a generic summary.

Retain the woman identified by her revived son, household relocation, sojourning and seven-year famine. Had spoken places the instruction before the ensuing return context; the Greek's famine has come is preserved rather than silently rewritten as a future prediction.
column3: How should the famine's aorist coming and seven-year duration relate to the command to leave; does the narrative require a flashback or a different temporal presentation?

column2: Retain obedience to Elisha, both woman and household, sojourning in the foreigners' land and seven years. Foreigners follows the selected designation without substituting a specific ethnic label at every occurrence.
Retain return after the full seven years, the selected to the city and appeal about both house and fields. No named city or account of who occupied her property is supplied.

Retain the king's conversation with Gehazi as Elisha's attendant and request for all the great deeds. The account's position after Gehazi's judgment is not reordered or supplied with an unstated healing explanation.

Retain the simultaneous revival narrative and presentative arrival of the woman, both house/fields claims, and identification of her living son. The son had been dead; revival is not changed into recovery from an illness that never involved death.

Retain the king's questioning, the woman's report, one eunuch and restoration of everything plus produce from departure to now. The singular field in the produce clause differs from earlier plural fields and remains; no unexpressed monetary calculation is added.
Retain Elisha's Damascus arrival, the son of Ader's illness and report that the man of God has come. The son-of-Ader designation is not replaced by a different conventional royal name.

Retain manaa as an unresolved item to carry, the meeting and inquiry of the Lord through the prophet concerning recovery. The king's illness is not given a diagnosis, and the transliterated term is not confidently equated with a grain offering.
column3: Does manaa mean a gift in this setting, and what evidence would justify replacing the transliteration with that natural English term?

column2: Retain Hazael's manaa, all the good things of Damascus, forty-camel load and the king's self-description as your son. The two uses of son have different functions, filial politeness and royal name; ordinary you addresses Elisha.

Retain the positive surely live message and the Lord's shown surely die statement, including the selected second-person death form. The contradiction and addressee boundary are not resolved by changing you to he or adding a negation absent here.
column3: Who is addressed by the second-person death prediction, and how do the life/death assurances relate without harmonizing a different source reading?

column2: Retain the compressed standing-before-face and holding-until-shame clauses, then the man of God's weeping. The exact actors and implied object are not supplied as settled names; held it refers provisionally to the face expression.
column3: Whose face is set or held, who becomes ashamed, and which subject governs each verb in this difficult sequence?

column2: Retain Hazael's question to my lord and all four predicted evils: burning strongholds, killing chosen men, dashing infants and tearing pregnant women. The violence remains restrained but explicit; no added motive or instruction is introduced.

Retain Hazael's self-description as a dead dog, not merely a dog, and Elisha's statement that the Lord has shown him reigning over Syria. The response indicates future position through the vision without explaining how succession occurs.
Retain Hazael's return, the master's question and the reported surely live response. The report omits the death statement, as does the selected text; the omission is not repaired in the quotation.

Retain machma, dipping in water, wrapping over his face, death and Hazael's succession. The verbs' agents and possessive referents are unexpressed; the inherited he wording does not explicitly resolve who applies the object or whose face is covered.
column3: What is machma, who performs the covering, and how should the pronouns be clarified without converting contextual inference into an explicit named actor in the Greek?

column2: Retain the fifth year of Israel's Joram son of Ahab and accession of Judah's Joram son of Jehoshaphat. The two same-named kings are distinguished by fathers and kingdoms; no additional co-regency clause is imported.
Retain age thirty-two and eight years in Jerusalem for Judah's king. These figures remain attached to the immediately preceding accession rather than being assigned to Israel's same-named ruler.
Retain the kings-of-Israel path, Ahab's house comparison and Ahab's daughter as wife, followed by evil before the Lord. The wife's personal name is not supplied here from a later notice.

Retain the Lord's unwillingness to destroy Judah because of David His slave and the lamp promise to him and his sons all the days. Lamp is explicit here and is not standardized to the different place/remnant expressions elsewhere.
Retain Edom's departure from beneath Judah's hand and making a king over themselves. The collective change of number is naturalized without identifying an unnamed Edomite ruler.

Retain Sior, all chariots, the king's rising and striking, encircling Edomites, chariot commanders and flight to dwellings. The selected verse does not explicitly say by night; the relation of the commanders to struck or encircled remains ambiguous in the inherited English.
column3: Are the chariot commanders additional objects of striking or people encircled with Joram, and which army is the fleeing people?

column2: Retain Edom's enduring break to this day and Lobena's break at that time. The two temporal statements remain distinct, and this day is the narrative's vantage rather than a modern political claim.
Retain the remaining acts, all Joram did, presentative and rhetorical daily-records reference for Judah's kings. The source title is not conflated with the parallel Israel annals formula.
Retain laying down with fathers, burial with fathers in David's city and Ahaziah's succession. David his father is dynastic wording; the text is not supplied with a new literal genealogy.
Retain Ahaziah son of Joram's accession in the twelfth year of Israel's Joram son of Ahab. The same-name distinction remains explicit; no harmonization with another accession notice is attempted.

Retain age twenty-two, one year in Jerusalem and Athaliah daughter of Omri king of Israel. Daughter is not silently expanded into granddaughter, and no alternate age is substituted from a parallel tradition.
Retain the repeated Ahab-house comparison and evil before the Lord. The selected shorter verse does not add a separate son-in-law explanation, so the inherited text remains concise.

Retain Hazael king of the foreigners, Remmoth-gilead and the Syrians striking Joram. The foreigner title is not replaced by Syria to harmonize the next verse; both selected designations remain visible.

Retain wounded Joram's return to Jezreel for treatment, Remmoth, Hazael king of Syria and Ahaziah's visit to Joram son of Ahab. The repeated names distinguish visitor and patient; no extra Judah title is supplied to the selected visitor clause.
